### To make things tidier and cleaner this is only code for Clam Counts and Prevalence. Polydora and Cliona will be addressed in seperate scripts.

```{r VariableSet, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Set your variables
Estuaries <- c("AB") # Limits to only Apalachicola Bay
Database = "OysterLocalMD20250821"  # Set the local database to use
Server = "localhost\\LOCALSQL" # Set the local Server to use
```

```{r DatabaseDownload}
# Connect to Local database server and pull all necessary data, then close connection 
con <- dbConnect(odbc(),
                    Driver = "SQL Server", 
                    Server = Server,
                    Database = Database,
                    Authentication = "ActiveDirectoryIntegrated")

hsdbShellPest <- tbl(con,in_schema("hsdb", "ShellPest")) %>%
  collect() %>%
  filter(substring(SampleEventID, 1, 2) %in% Estuaries)

hsdbConditionIndex <- tbl(con,in_schema("hsdb", "ConditionIndex")) %>%
  collect() %>%
  filter(substring(SampleEventID, 1, 2) %in% Estuaries)

DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

```{r DataFiltersBasic}
# Adjust data to include necessary fields and exclude incomplete years.
ShellPest <- hsdbShellPest %>% 
  mutate(Section = substring(OysterID, 3, 3),
         FixedLocation = substring(SampleEventID, 19, 22),
         Year = substring(SampleEventID, 8, 11),
         Month = substring(SampleEventID, 12, 13),
         Day = substr(SampleEventID, 14, 15),
         Date = as.Date(paste(Year, Month, Day, sep = "-")),
         Season = case_when(
          month(Date) >= 1 & month(Date) <= 3 ~ "Winter",
          month(Date) >= 4 & month(Date) <= 6 ~ "Spring",
          month(Date) >= 7 & month(Date) <= 9 ~ "Summer",
          month(Date) >= 10 & month(Date) <= 12 ~ "Fall",
          TRUE ~ "Invalid")) %>%
  left_join(hsdbConditionIndex, by = c("OysterID")) %>%
  filter(Year < 2023) %>%
  select(OysterID,
         PhotoSurface,
         TotalArea,
         ClamCount,
         Section,
         FixedLocation,
         Date,
         Month,
         Year,
         Season,
         ProcessedBy,
         ShellHeight,
         TotalWeight) 

# Adjust to provide the sum values needed for calculations
ShellPest1 <- ShellPest %>%
  group_by(OysterID,
           Section,
           FixedLocation,
           Date,
           Month,
           Year,
           Season,
           ProcessedBy,
           ShellHeight,
           TotalWeight) %>%
  summarise(TotalSurfaceArea = sum(TotalArea, na.rm = TRUE),
         TotalExternalArea = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 2, 2) == "E", TotalArea, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         TotalInternalArea = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 2, 2) == "I", TotalArea, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         TotalTopArea = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 1, 1) == "T", TotalArea, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         TotalBottomArea = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 1, 1) == "B", TotalArea, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
        # Clam counts
         TotalClamCount = sum(ClamCount, na.rm = TRUE),
         ClamCountExternal = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 2, 2) == "E", ClamCount, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         ClamCountInternal = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 2, 2) == "I", ClamCount, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         ClamCountTop = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 1, 1) == "T", ClamCount, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         ClamCountBottom = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 1, 1) == "B", ClamCount, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         .groups = "drop"   # removes grouping after summarise
         ) 

ShellPest2 <- ShellPest1 %>% # getting everything that needs to be scaled
  mutate(TotalWeight_scaled = scale(TotalWeight)[,1],
         ShellHeight_scaled = scale(ShellHeight)[,1],
         Year_scaled = scale(as.numeric(Year))[,1]  # Scaled for better convergence
          ) %>% # getting everything that needs to be factored or numeric
  mutate(Section = factor(Section, levels = c("W", "C", "E")),
         Season = factor(Season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")),
         Month = factor(Month, levels = 1:12, labels = month.abb),
         Year = factor(Year),   # Categorical for non-linear trends
         Year_numeric = as.numeric(as.character(Year)),  # For linear trends
         ProcessedBy = factor(ProcessedBy),
         FixedLocation = factor(FixedLocation)
         )

# Create binary infection status (0 = uninfected, 1 = infected)
ShellPest2$Infected <- ifelse(ShellPest2$TotalClamCount > 0, 1, 0)

# separate by year
year_breaks <- seq(as.Date("2016-01-01"), as.Date("2022-01-01"), by = "years")
year_labels <- format(year_breaks, "%Y")

# Assign CB friendly colors to sections and years
Section.colors <- c("W" = "#00a884", 
                    "C" = "#FF7979", 
                    "E" = "#6D9DFF")
yr.colors <- c("2016"="#FFBBBB",
               "2017"="#56B4E9",
               "2018"="#CC79A7",
               "2019"="#0067A0",
               "2021"="#58FF7E",
               "2022"="#FF6666")
Season.colors <- c("Winter"="#FFBBBB",
               "Spring"="#56B4E9",
               "Summer"="#CC79A7",
               "Fall"="#0067A0")

# Remove unnecessary dataframes
rm(hsdbConditionIndex, hsdbShellPest, ShellPest, ShellPest1)

```

``` {r Initial GLMM Models}

# Additional optimization options if convergence issues occur:
# control = glmmTMBControl(
#   optimizer = optim,
#   optArgs = list(method = "BFGS"),
#   start = list(theta = log(1)),  # Starting values for dispersion
#   map = list(),  # Fix parameters if needed
#   optCtrl = list(eval.max = 1000, iter.max = 1000)
# )

##### Section ONLY as a fixed effect
model.S <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

##### TotalWeight ONLY as a fixed effect 
model.TW <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ TotalWeight_scaled,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

##### ShellHeight ONLY as a fixed effect 
model.SH <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ ShellHeight_scaled,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

##### Section AND TotalWeight as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

##### Section AND ShellHeight as a fixed effect 
model.S.SH <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + ShellHeight_scaled,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

##### TotalWeight AND ShellHeight as a fixed effect 
model.TW.SH <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ TotalWeight_scaled + ShellHeight_scaled,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

### Use AICc to compare the 2 models: we'll use the model with the lowest score for making any inferences moving forward
model.names1 <- c('SectionOnly', 
                 'TotalWeightOnly', 
                 'ShellHeightOnly', 
                 'Section+TotalWeight', 
                 'Section+SH',
                 'TotalWeight+SH')
aictab(list(model.S, 
            model.TW, 
            model.SH, 
            model.S.TW, 
            model.S.SH,
            model.TW.SH), 
       modnames = model.names1) #will use one for analysis

######### Since Section&TotalWeight has a Massively better AICc, only it will be tested here
best_model1 <- model.S.TW
#########

##### Assess goodness-of-fit
simulateResiduals(best_model1, n = 250, refit = FALSE, plot = TRUE)

# Calculate R-squared equivalent for count models. Closer to 1 is better
r2(best_model1)

##### Look at estimates
summary(best_model1)

# Remove unnecesssary models
rm(model.S, model.S.SH, model.S.TW, model.SH, model.TW, model.TW.SH)

```

``` {r Improving Basic GLMM Models}
# Extended model set: Adding Season and Year systematically

##### Baseline - Best model from above
### Section AND TotalWeight as a fixed effect 
# model.S.TW <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled,
#                    ziformula = ~1,
#                    family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
#                    data = ShellPest2)

# Add Season (cyclical pattern)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Season as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Ss <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

# Add Year as a factor (non-linear temporal trend)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Year as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Y <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Year,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

# Add Year as a linear trend (more parsimonious)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Year_scaled as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Y_s <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Year_scaled,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

# Add Season AND Year (factor)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Season AND Year as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Ss.Y <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season + Year,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

# Add Season AND Year (linear)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Season AND Year_Scaled as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Ss.Y_s <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season + Year_scaled,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

# Add Season-Year interaction (test if seasonal patterns change over years)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Season-Year_scaled interaction as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Ss.X.Y_s <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season * Year_scaled,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

### Use AICc to compare the 2 models: we'll use the model with the lowest score for making any inferences moving forward
model.names2 <- c('1-SectionWeight (Base)', 
                 '2-SectionWeight+Season', 
                 '3-SectionWeight+Year', 
                 '4-SectionWeight+YearScaled', 
                 '5-SectionWeight+Season+Year',
                 '6-SectionWeight+Season+YearScaled',
                 '7-SectionWeight+Season * YearScaled'
                 )
aictab(list(bestmodel1, 
            model.S.TW.Ss, 
            model.S.TW.Y, 
            model.S.TW.Y_s, 
            model.S.TW.Ss.Y,
            model.S.TW.Ss.Y_s,
            model.S.TW.Ss.X.Y_s), 
       modnames = model.names2) #will use one for analysis

######### Since SectionWeight+Season+Year has a significantly better AICc, only it will be tested here
best_model2 <- model.S.TW.Ss.Y
#########

##### Assess goodness-of-fit
simulateResiduals(best_model2, n = 175, refit = FALSE, plot = TRUE)

# Check for temporal autocorrelation since we have time series data
acf(residuals(best_model2, type = "pearson"))
# The residuals exhibit no significant autocorrelation, implying that the model has effectively captured the temporal dependencies. 

# Calculate R-squared equivalent for count models. Closer to 1 is better
r2(best_model2)

##### Look at estimates
summary(best_model2)

# Key findings from model selection
print("=== MODEL SELECTION INSIGHTS ===")
print("1. Both Season AND Year are highly important (5 >> 2 or 3 alone)")
print("2. Non-linear year effects are crucial (5 >> 6: factor vs linear year)")
print("3. Seasonal patterns are consistent across years (5 >> 7: no interaction needed)")
print("4. Temporal factors explain MASSIVE variation (ΔAICc = 156 vs baseline)")

# Remove unnecessary models

rm(model.S.TW.Ss, model.S.TW.Y, model.S.TW.Y_s, model.S.TW.Ss.Y, model.S.TW.Ss.Y_s, model.S.TW.Ss.X.Y_s)

```

``` {r Prevalence Seasonal & Yearly Patterns}
# Analyze prevalence seasonal and yearly patterns in detail

# 1. SEASONAL PATTERNS
print("=== PREVALENCE SEASONAL PATTERNS ===")
P.season_emm <- emmeans(P.best_model2, ~ Season, type = "response")
P.season_results <- as.data.frame(P.season_emm) %>%
  rename(lower_col = asymp.LCL,
         upper_col = asymp.UCL)
print(P.season_results)

# Plot seasonal effects

P.season_pattern <- ggplot(P.season_results, aes(x = Season, y = prob)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_col, ymax = upper_col), width = 0.2, linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence Seasonal Pattern in Clam Counts", 
       subtitle = "Estimated marginal means ± 95% CI",
       y = "Prevalence of Clam", x = "Season") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 12))

print(P.season_pattern)

# Calculate seasonal fold-differences
P.max_season <- P.season_results[which.max(P.season_results$prob), ]
P.min_season <- P.season_results[which.min(P.season_results$prob), ]
P.seasonal_ratio <- P.max_season$prob / P.min_season$prob
print(paste("Peak season (", P.max_season$Season, ") has", round(P.seasonal_ratio, 2), 
            "higher prevalence of clams than lowest season (", P.min_season$Season, ")"))


# 2. YEARLY PATTERNS  
print("=== PREVALENCE YEARLY PATTERNS ===")
P.year_emm <- emmeans(P.best_model2, ~ Year, type = "response")
P.year_results <- as.data.frame(P.year_emm) 
print(P.year_results)

P.year_pattern <- ggplot(P.year_results, aes(x = Year, y = prob)) +
  geom_line(size = 1, color = "darkred") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "darkred") +
  geom_errorbar(aes_string(ymin = lower_col, ymax = upper_col), width = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Year-to-Year Variation in Clam Prevalence", 
       subtitle = "Non-linear temporal trend",
       y = "Predicted Clam Prevalence", x = "Year") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 12))

print(P.year_pattern)

# Calculate yearly variation
P.max_year <- P.year_results[which.max(P.year_results$emmean), ]
P.min_year <- P.year_results[which.min(P.year_results$emmean), ]
P.yearly_ratio <- P.max_year$emmean / P.min_year$emmean
print(paste("Highest year (", P.max_year$Year, ") had", round(P.yearly_ratio, 2), 
            "times more clams than least year (", P.min_year$Year, ")"))

# 3. PREVALENCE SECTION PATTERNS  
print("=== PREVALENCE SECTION PATTERNS ===")
P.section_emm <- emmeans(P.best_model2, ~ Section, type = "response")
P.section_results <- as.data.frame(P.section_emm) 
print(P.section_results)

P.section_pattern <- ggplot(P.section_results, aes(x = Section, y = prob)) +
  geom_line(size = 1, color = "darkred") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "darkred") +
  geom_errorbar(aes_string(ymin = lower_col, ymax = upper_col), width = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "section-to-section Variation in Clam Prevalence", 
       subtitle = "Non-linear temporal trend",
       y = "Predicted Clam Prevalence", x = "section") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 12))

print(P.section_pattern)

# Calculate sectionly variation
P.max_section <- P.section_results[which.max(P.section_results$prob), ]
P.min_section <- P.section_results[which.min(P.section_results$prob), ]
P.sectionly_ratio <- (P.max_section$prob - P.min_section$prob) * 100
print(paste("Highest section (", P.max_section$Section, ") had", round(P.sectionly_ratio, 2), 
            "% higher prevalence than least section (", P.min_section$Section, ")"))

```

``` {r Bias Testing}
# QUALITY CONTROL ANALYSIS: Testing for Observer and Location Bias

# Check for potential confounding
print("\n=== CONFOUNDING CHECK ===")
print("Staff members by year (check if staff changed over time):")
staff_year <- table(ShellPest2$ProcessedBy, ShellPest2$Year)
print(staff_year)

print("\nStaff members by section (check if staff specialized in certain sections):")
staff_section <- table(ShellPest2$ProcessedBy, ShellPest2$Section)
print(staff_section)

print("\nFixed locations by year (check if locations changed over time):")
location_year <- table(ShellPest2$FixedLocation, ShellPest2$Year)
print(location_year[1:min(10, nrow(location_year)), ])  # Show first 10 locations

# BIAS TESTING MODELS
# OBSERVER BIAS TESTING 
# Test 1: Add ProcessedBy to count model
model.B1_observer <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season + Year + ProcessedBy,
                            ziformula = ~ 1,
                            family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                            data = ShellPest2)

# Test 2: Add ProcessedBy to prevalence model
model.P_observer <- glmmTMB(Infected ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season + Year + ProcessedBy,
                           family = binomial,
                           data = ShellPest2,
                           control = glmmTMBControl(optimizer = optim,
                                                  optArgs = list(method = "BFGS")))

# LOCATION BIAS TESTING
# Test 3: Add FixedLocation as random effect (nested within Section) to count model
model.B2_location <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season + Year + (1|FixedLocation),
                            ziformula = ~ 1,
                            family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                            data = ShellPest2)

# Test 4: Add FixedLocation as random effect (nested within Section) to prevalence model
model.P_location <- glmmTMB(Infected ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season + Year + (1|FixedLocation),
                           family = binomial,
                           data = ShellPest2,
                           control = glmmTMBControl(optimizer = optim,
                                                  optArgs = list(method = "BFGS")))

# COMBINED BIAS TESTING 
# Test 5: Both observer and location effects on counts
model.B3_both <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season + Year + ProcessedBy + (1|FixedLocation),
                        ziformula = ~ 1,
                        family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                        data = ShellPest2)

# Test 6: Both observer and location effects on prevalence
model.P_both <- glmmTMB(Infected ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season + Year + ProcessedBy + (1|FixedLocation),
                       family = binomial,
                       data = ShellPest2,
                       control = glmmTMBControl(optimizer = optim,
                                              optArgs = list(method = "BFGS")))


##### Assess goodness-of-fit (counts)
simulateResiduals(model.B3_both, n = 175, refit = FALSE, plot = TRUE)

# Check for temporal autocorrelation since we have time series data
acf(residuals(model.B3_both, type = "pearson"))
# The residuals exhibit no significant autocorrelation, implying that the model has effectively captured the temporal dependencies. 

# Calculate R-squared equivalent for count models. Closer to 1 is better
r2(model.B3_both)

##### Look at estimates
summary(model.B3_both)

##### Assess goodness-of-fit (prevalence)
simulateResiduals(model.P_both, n = 175, refit = FALSE, plot = TRUE)

# Check for temporal autocorrelation since we have time series data
acf(residuals(model.P_both, type = "pearson"))
# The residuals exhibit no significant autocorrelation, implying that the model has effectively captured the temporal dependencies. 

# Calculate R-squared equivalent for prevalence models. Closer to 0 is better
r2(model.P_both)

##### Look at estimates
summary(model.P_both)


# MODEL COMPARISON: Original vs Bias-corrected models
# For COUNT models
count_bias_models <- list(
  "Original" = best_model2,  # Your best original model
  "Observer_Bias" = model.B1_observer,
  "Location_Bias" = model.B2_location, 
  "Both_Biases" = model.B3_both
)

count_bias_comparison <- aictab(count_bias_models)
print("COUNT MODEL BIAS COMPARISON:")
print(count_bias_comparison)

# For PREVALENCE models
prev_bias_models <- list(
  "Original" = P.best_model2,  # Assuming P4 was your best prevalence model
  "Observer_Bias" = model.P_observer,
  "Location_Bias" = model.P_location,
  "Both_Biases" = model.P_both
)

prev_bias_comparison <- aictab(prev_bias_models)
print("PREVALENCE MODEL BIAS COMPARISON:")
print(prev_bias_comparison)

# STATISTICAL TESTS for bias significance
print("\n=== SIGNIFICANCE TESTS ===")

# Test 1: Is ProcessedBy significant?
observer_count_test <- anova(best_model2, model.B1_observer)
print("Observer effect on COUNT model:")
print(observer_count_test)

observer_prev_test <- anova(P.best_model2, model.P_observer)
print("Observer effect on PREVALENCE model:")
print(observer_prev_test)

# Test 2: Is FixedLocation significant?
location_count_test <- anova(best_model2, model.B2_location)
print("Location effect on COUNT model:")
print(location_count_test)

location_prev_test <- anova(P.best_model2, model.P_location)
print("Location effect on PREVALENCE model:")
print(location_prev_test)

# EFFECT SIZE ANALYSIS
print("\n=== OBSERVER BIAS MAGNITUDE ===")
observer_effects_count <- emmeans(model.B1_observer, ~ ProcessedBy, type = "response")
  print("Count differences by observer:")
  observer_count_df <- as.data.frame(observer_effects_count)
  print(observer_count_df)
  
  # Calculate fold differences between observers
  max_observer <- max(observer_count_df$response)
  min_observer <- 0.01
  observer_bias_ratio <- max_observer / min_observer
  print(paste("Maximum observer bias:", round(observer_bias_ratio, 2), "fold difference"))

  # Calculate variation between locations
  print("\n=== LOCATION VARIABILITY ===")
if(any(grepl("Location", count_bias_comparison$Modnames[1:2]))) {
  # Extract random effect variance for FixedLocation
  location_variance <- VarCorr(model.B2_location)
  print("FixedLocation random effect variance:")
  print(location_variance)
}





importance_table <- function(full_model, predictors) {
  # intercept-only null model
  null_mod <- update(full_model, . ~ 1)
  
  # Full model pseudo-R²
  pseudoR2 <- function(model, null_model = NULL) {
    ll_full <- as.numeric(logLik(model))
    if (is.null(null_model)) {
      null_model <- update(model, . ~ 1)
    }
    ll_null <- as.numeric(logLik(null_model))
    1 - (ll_full / ll_null)
  }
  R2_full <- pseudoR2(full_model, null_mod)
  
  # Function for each predictor
  drop_one_safe <- function(var, full) {
    # reduced model
    reduced <- tryCatch(
      update(full, as.formula(paste(". ~ . -", var))),
      error = function(e) NULL,
      warning = function(w) {invokeRestart("muffleWarning")}
    )
    if (is.null(reduced)) {
      return(data.frame(
        Predictor = var,
        deltaAIC = NA, LRT = NA, df_diff = NA, p_value = NA,
        R2_full = R2_full, R2_reduced = NA, deltaR2 = NA,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      ))
    }
    
    # logLik + AIC
    ll_full <- as.numeric(logLik(full))
    ll_red  <- as.numeric(logLik(reduced))
    aic_full <- AIC(full)
    aic_red  <- AIC(reduced)
    deltaAIC <- aic_red - aic_full
    
    # parameter df
    df_full <- attr(logLik(full), "df")
    df_red  <- attr(logLik(reduced), "df")
    if (is.null(df_full)) df_full <- length(coef(full)$cond)
    if (is.null(df_red))  df_red  <- length(coef(reduced)$cond)
    
    df_diff <- as.integer(round(df_full - df_red))
    LRT <- 2 * (ll_full - ll_red)
    p_value <- if (!is.na(df_diff) && df_diff > 0) {
      pchisq(LRT, df = df_diff, lower.tail = FALSE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
    
    # pseudo R²
    R2_reduced <- pseudoR2(reduced, null_mod)
    deltaR2 <- R2_full - R2_reduced
    
    data.frame(
      Predictor = var,
      deltaAIC = deltaAIC,
      LRT = LRT,
      df_diff = df_diff,
      p_value = p_value,
      R2_full = R2_full,
      R2_reduced = R2_reduced,
      deltaR2 = deltaR2,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }
  
  # Build table
  results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(predictors, drop_one_safe, full = full_model))
  results <- results %>% arrange(desc(deltaR2))
  return(results)
}

predictors <- c("Section", "TotalWeight_scaled", "Season", "Year", "ProcessedBy")

importance_results <- importance_table(model.B3_both, predictors)

importance_results

```


``` {r Seasonal & Yearly Patterns}
# The following code is only needed if there is not significant bias found above

stop()

# Analyze seasonal and yearly patterns in detail

# 1. SEASONAL PATTERNS
print("=== SEASONAL PATTERNS ===")
season_emm <- emmeans(best_model2, ~ Season, type = "response")
season_results <- as.data.frame(season_emm) %>%
  rename(lower_col = asymp.LCL,
         upper_col = asymp.UCL)
print(season_results)

# Plot seasonal effects

season_pattern <- ggplot(season_results, aes(x = Season, y = response)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_col, ymax = upper_col), width = 0.2, linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Seasonal Pattern in Clam Counts", 
       subtitle = "Estimated marginal means ± 95% CI",
       y = "Predicted Clam Count", x = "Season") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 12))

print(season_pattern)

# Calculate seasonal fold-differences
max_season <- season_results[which.max(season_results$response), ]
min_season <- season_results[which.min(season_results$response), ]
seasonal_ratio <- max_season$response / min_season$response
print(paste("Peak season (", max_season$Season, ") has", round(seasonal_ratio, 2), 
            "times more clams than lowest season (", min_season$Season, ")"))


# 2. YEARLY PATTERNS  
print("=== YEARLY PATTERNS ===")
year_emm <- emmeans(best_model2, ~ Year, type = "response")
year_results <- as.data.frame(year_emm) 
print(year_results)

year_pattern <- ggplot(year_results, aes(x = Year, y = response)) +
  geom_line(size = 1, color = "darkred") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "darkred") +
  geom_errorbar(aes_string(ymin = lower_col, ymax = upper_col), width = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Year-to-Year Variation in Clam Counts", 
       subtitle = "Non-linear temporal trend",
       y = "Predicted Clam Count", x = "Year") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 12))

print(year_pattern)

# Calculate yearly variation
max_year <- year_results[which.max(year_results$response), ]
min_year <- year_results[which.min(year_results$response), ]
yearly_ratio <- max_year$response / min_year$response
print(paste("Highest year (", max_year$Year, ") had", round(yearly_ratio, 2), 
            "times more clams than least year (", min_year$Year, ")"))
```
